comments.text: Tornado swarms are awful. I tend to watch live coverage across the midwest when these breakouts occur on Hall Y'all.  2, 3 or 4 days without power isn't a good thing to have to live with.  8, 10, 12 days in the Deep South aren't fun either.  Hot, muggy, everyone that has a generator has filled several small 30 to 40 gallon tanks with gaso ahead of time.  Natural gas powered fixed generators are commonplace in yards all across my region of the state.  As much preparation as you can do, it seems it's never enough.  Exactly 10 years ago we were in the middle of a major flood across the south of my state.  2 1/2 days of steady but varying rates of rainfall that never stopped.  Power outages everywhere because a huge weather radar red blob of rain didn't move, didn't stop raining for almost 60 hours.  The lakes drainage basin had flooded way past its capacity to hold water....the wind blew water back into the lakes in the east for 5 more days, those same winds from the southeast were not allowing lakes and small rivers and bayous to drain the western south half of the state.  The Cajun Navy found its true calling that week and turned out by the thousands doing rescues in situations that were horrible.  Have we been seeing the results of continued weather manipulation for far too long?  Mankind's arrogance.
